It would be interesting to see how many can trudge through a multi-year bear market though (so far this hasn’t happened to most Indian investors). That would be tough for anyone.

posts.author: RupeeRiser
posts.text: This is Why Enterprise Trading Platforms Need Best Bid/Ask P&L Calculation (Not Just LTP) — Currently, most trading platforms calculate live P&L on positions using Last Traded Price (LTP) . This gives traders a misleading view of their actual profit/loss. The Problem: LTP-based P&L doesn’t reflect realizable value. Creates a misleading perception of profit or loss, causing traders to make decisions based on fiction rather than factual, executable market data. The Solution: Platforms should offer an option to calculate P&L based on: Best Bid (for long positions) - what you can actually sell at.…

posts.author: pavinjoseph
posts.text: Bear Put spread , is it to better to book profit now — Your thesis has come true, but the trade hasn’t paid off as you expected. A bear put spread has some negative theta, so holding it longer would eat away at your premium. To profit more off this trade you need: either a continuation of the move downward hold it to expiry (dangerous as you could take max loss) and have the index stay well below the BEP. Give yourself more time to be right next time - choose monthly or next month expiry. Target 50% of the max profit. Close the trade at the midpoint of the contract duration.

When we buy an ATM Call and sell an ATM Put of the same strike and expiry, we are basically creating a synthetic futures/forward position. So, if before expiry the Spot moves up by 400 points but the Futures moves only 200 points, I would expect the synthetic position to be closer to the 200-point futures move , rather than the full 400-point spot move. Don’t focus only on win rate one big move can wipe out many small profits.

Most legitimate loan/banking apps have IPV (In-Person/Video Verification)where they take a video and ask questions for additional verification. However, I’m not sure how easily this can be bypassed, especially with some questionable Chinese loan apps or similar apps that provide loans with minimal verification. It’s also possible that you recently updated your KYC details somewhere else, and that update was synced with the CKYC system. So, it doesn’t necessarily mean that a new account was opened or that anything suspicious happened. However, if you’re still a bit cautious, it’s better to contact Sharekhan and confirm what exactly was updated.

posts.author: Ranjit_DailyTrader
posts.text: Are Technical Indicators a Trading Edge or Just Noise? — They can improve trading, but only if you understand what each one is actually telling you. Using too many indicators at the same time can definitely create confusion. For me, Market Profile and Order Flow are more useful for understanding where buyers and sellers are active, while VWAP helps identify the broader intraday bias. RSI can be useful as an additional confirmation, but I wouldn’t use it alone for entries. The key is to have a clear setup and rules. More indicators don’t mean better trades—better interpretation does.

posts.author: Ranjit_DailyTrader
posts.text: What is entry and exit point on Order flow chart — I look for strong buying/selling aggression, absorption, and a clear shift in order flow around important support/resistance levels. I don’t enter just because I see high volume. I prefer to see price accept the level and order flow continue in the same direction rather than entering on the first spike. If the order flow that supported my entry gets completely absorbed or reverses, that’s my signal that the trade idea is invalid. I usually book partial profits at the first major level and trail the remaining position if the order flow continue…

posts.text: Does GSEC worth for 3 Year Investment than FD? — Historically bond MF were favored because of better tax treatment, now most of that advantage is gone. In higher tax bracket debt MF still has some advantage as you pay tax on FD interest every year, against MF where you pay tax only on redemption, so you can let money compound. Also, MF provides better liquidity compared to FD as you ca take out money any time, without any penalties. And over a longer cycle debt MF will offer slightly better returns than FD. But yeah not a lot of advantage now, as the taxation has changed.

posts.author: KarthikAcharya
posts.text: Deep ITM Options — Hi Amit, Yes, you can place buy/sell orders in deep ITM options. However, if the option is illiquid, your order will execute only if there’s a counterparty available at your price. For illiquid options, a limit order is generally preferable to a market order. If there’s no buyer/seller at your specified price, the order will remain unexecuted. Hence, if it’s a stock option, they are physically settled if they expire ITM, while index options will be cash-settled.

posts.author: Adarsh_Patil
posts.text: Liquidity issue related query — If the strike stays OTM, it will expire worthless and there will be no physical delivery obligation. If it turns ITM and there is no liquidity to exit, it can result in a physical delivery obligation. You can buy the stock on expiry day, which will be netted off against the delivery obligation. Alternatively, buying the corresponding futures position should also work. With CAS, you get an additional 10 minutes after the closing price is determined, so you can assess whether the option has turned ITM and take action accordingly.

posts.author: Quicko
posts.text: Taxation of Debt Mutual Funds and Conservative Hybrid Funds (Section 50AA of the Income Tax Act) — If the debt mutual fund has been sold on or after 1st April, 2023 the gains arising from those redemption will be treated as STCG and would be taxable at slab rate irrespective of the period of holding. The benefit of rebate udner section 87A would be available against such STCG.

posts.author: Quicko
posts.text: Gifting MF units in Zerodha — Yes, if the mutual funds are invested in your daughter’s name from the beginning, no transfer is required when she turns 18 and no tax arises on you or your wife or grandparents. No. A gift of mutual fund units from a parent is tax-exempt in the hands of the daughter; tax arises only when she sells them. The original cost of acquisition and holding period are carried forward; she does not get fresh units at the transfer-day NAV. Her cost will remain ₹10 per unit (your original purchase price), and capital gains will be computed accordingly when she sells them.

posts.author: Quicko
posts.text: FIFO rule transferred shares — Cpaital gains are always calculated on FIFO basis. That is why the shares which were purchased earlier would be considered for calculating capital gains even though they were later on transferred to separate demat account.

posts.author: Quicko
posts.text: Intraday trade on 30/3/2026 (settled 2/4/2026) — trade date or settlement date for tax FY 2025-26 — Trade date is considered for the purpose of reporting in ITR. Since the trade was carried out on the same day it would be considered as Intraday only. Brokers in their report consider settlement date. You can manually adjust that entry and show it as an Intraday.

posts.author: Quicko
posts.text: Tax on debt and fund of funds — Hello @tax007 Capital gains from US Stock or funds of Indian AMC investing in US market would not be treated as debt funds and hence the changes in capital gains for pre and post April 2023 would not be applicable. The taxability depends on the period of holding if the funds have been held for less than 24 months then it would be treated as STCG taxable at slab rates otherwise LTCG taxable at 12.5%. If the gains are STCG taxable at slab rates then benefit of rebate under 87A would be applicable.

posts.author: Quicko
posts.text: FIFO rule transferred shares — It would not be considered as sales because it is just a transfer from demat to another demat. However it would reflect in the profit and loss statement. You can ignore such transaction in the calculations of capital gains.

A small-cap index would give a closer hedge, but liquidity becomes the bigger question. If the underlying stocks themselves aren’t very liquid, the index derivative may end up being thinly traded too. Not sure if there’s enough actual hedging demand first. Otherwise, we could end…

posts.author: Quicko
posts.text: Can STCG of equity be shown in 44AD? — Hey @sachindei65 STCG can potentially be treated as business income if the taxpayer treats the securities as stock-in-trade rather than capital assets. In that case, the income would be reported as business income instead of capital gains. If you want to report the business income under Section 44AD, you can declare the total sales as Gross Receipts/Revenue. The profit to be declared under the presumptive scheme should be 6% of eligible digital receipts or 8% of other receipts, or the actual profit, whichever is higher. Thanks

posts.author: KaranAggarwal
posts.text: What’s the Best Way to Create a Monthly Budget? — For budgeting the basic formula of 50/30/20 rule is a good starting point, but it need not be followed rigidly. A practical approach is to first cover essential expenses, set aside savings and investments, and then use the remaining amount for discretionary spending. I suggest reviewing the budget once a month is good enough. For automation you may check tools such as Money Manager, Wallet by BudgetBakers, and Goodbudget which can help you track expenses and set spending limits.

posts.author: cvs
posts.text: Global Investing — They absolutely do waive them off. (and it’s not an one-off anecdote either.) That’s the negotiating upfront bit i was referring to. Of course it is easier if one has remittance volume or already pays (directly/indirectly) for other services at the bank. (which the bank will lose if you switch to using another bank just due to your forex needs). That and minimising the intermediaries involved (payment processors, multiple bank branches, other banks) have anecdotally been the key factors to ensure fast and reliable foreign remittances (in either direction).

posts.text: Scanner on Streak — Please note that the quantity for a backtest is automatically determined based on the initial capital. The quantity is calculated as: Initial Capital ÷ Stock Price = Quantity For example, if the initial capital is ₹10,000 and the stock price is ₹1,000, the quantity will be 10. If you want the quantity to be 1, you can keep the initial capital as ₹0* By default, the backtest will then consider the quantity as 1. posts.author: Ranjit_DailyTrader
posts.text: Help with some trading conditions — You can combine both conditions in the trigger: the close must freshly cross above the Supertrend , and at the same time the close must be below the 20 EMA . In simple terms, trigger only when Close crosses above Supertrend AND Close < EMA(20) . This will avoid signals where the price is already above the Supertrend or above the 20 EMA.

posts.author: Ranjit_DailyTrader
posts.text: What Signals Do You Focus on in Order Flow? — I mainly focus on delta, bid/ask imbalance, absorption, and volume around key levels like VWAP, VPOC, and previous highs/lows . I look for aggressive buying or selling and then check whether price actually follows that activity. For example, strong selling with no downside movement can indicate absorption, while a strong imbalance followed by a clean breakout gives more confirmation. I prefer combining these signals with price action rather than relying on a single footprint signal.

posts.author: RajendraPatil
posts.text: Buying Index fund NIFTY 50 For long term — Would you be open to exploring another index for a very long-term horizon? The Nifty LargeMidcap 250 could be a stronger alternative to a plain vanilla Nifty 50 fund. It combines the top 100 large-caps with 150 mid-caps in a 50:50 split. Because it mechanically rebalances every quarter, it naturally executes an automated “buy low, sell high” approach. posts.text: ORIENTCABL shares — Hey @sandeep_cs , the ₹272 was the IPO issue price, while the stock listed/opened at ₹450 on NSE. The ₹450 became the reference price for the initial trading band, so the circuit isn’t calculated from the ₹272 IPO price. So, with a 10% band: ₹450 × 10% = ₹45 Lower circuit = ₹450 − ₹45 = ₹405 Upper circuit = ₹450 + ₹45 = ₹495 And ₹405 is 48.9% above the IPO price of ₹272: ₹405 − ₹272 = ₹133 ₹133 ÷ ₹272 × 100 = 48.9% Basically, the stock listed at a big premium of ₹450 vs ₹272, and the circuit is then calculated from the ₹450 listing price. posts.author: DrorH
posts.text: GSEC 10 Year Yield — Nice that you got in at the auction, sandeep. If 7.2% already looks good and 8% is the hope, a middle path for the rest is to split it: some at the next auctions, more if it really gets to 7.8-8%. Waiting for the exact top usually ends with buying nothing. SDLs are worth comparing too, since state loans normally yield a little more than a G-sec of similar tenor. Interest on both is taxed at your slab rate, so in the 30% bracket a 7.2% G-sec nets closer to 5%, and that’s the figure to set against FDs or equity.

posts.text: VWAP + Order Flow vs. Indicators: Which Actually Gives Better Options Entries? — I personally don’t use RSI, MACD or too many other indicators. I prefer keeping things simple and trust the mean/average to give me a sense of trend. I mostly use 9 EMA and 27 EMA on a 15-min chart. When they cross, I wait for the candle to close and then look for an entry in the direction of the crossover. Bearish crossover, I look for a put side entry, and bullish crossover, I look for a call side entry. I find it much cleaner than trying to combine too many indicators.

posts.author: Quicko
posts.text: Taxation clarification on gifting MFs — Hi @sandeep0604 Under Section 64(1)(iv), income arising to your spouse from assets transferred by you directly or indirectly, otherwise than for adequate consideration, is required to be clubbed with your income. So in your case: You own the foreign FoFs. You transfer them to your wife without consideration. Your wife subsequently sells them and earns LTCG. Even though the sale happens from her account, the resulting capital gain would generally be clubbed in your ITR, rather than being taxed only in her ITR. posts.author: trade360
posts.text: How Can Market Profile Help You Identify Where the Market Is Likely to Reverse? — I usually watch how price behaves around VAH and VAL. If price breaks above VAH but quickly falls back into the value area, I’d look for a short setup once it shows weakness, with a stop above the failed breakout high. Similarly, if price breaks below VAL and reclaims it, I’d watch for a long entry. POC can act as a target when price moves back into value. For me, we should wait for confirmation and avoid trading every breakout.

posts.author: trade360
posts.text: How Can Order Flow Reveal a False Breakout Before the Market Reverses? — I think the key is to see how price reacts after the breakout, not just the increase in volume. If aggressive buying isn’t pushing the price higher despite strong delta, it could be a sign of sellers absorbing that demand. That’s where things get interesting.

posts.author: Edwin_Marshall
posts.text: How Can Order Flow Reveal a False Breakout Before the Market Reverses? — Big sellers absorbed all the buying at resistance using passive limit orders. Once buyers dried up, price collapsed under trapped stop-losses.

posts.author: Edwin_Marshall
posts.text: How Can Market Profile Help You Identify Where the Market Is Likely to Reverse? — Fast moves out of value that fail lead to fast moves to the other side of value. Don’t chase breakouts blindly. Wait to see if time builds outside the Value Area. If no time builds, trade the move back to POC.

posts.author: Gagan_suryaputra
posts.text: Coffee Can Portfolio Performance — The biggest challenge with a 1,000-stock portfolio would be knowing when to sell, not when to buy. A few multibaggers can make the overall returns look great, even if a large chunk of the portfolio underperforms. I’d be curious to see the returns after accounting for dead stocks, delisted companies and the time spent holding them. Survivorship bias can make a coffee-can portfolio look much better in hindsight than it felt while building it.

posts.author: Gagan_suryaputra
posts.text: Can We Predict the Stock Market's Next Move Amid Global Uncertainty? — A rise in US yields might pressure valuations across the market, while banks could react differently depending on bond yields, deposit growth and credit demand. I’d watch the rupee, US bond yields, crude and FII index-futures positioning before the open, but use price action after the open to judge which factor the market is actually reacting to. The headlines give you the possible direction; they don’t tell you how much is already priced in.

posts.author: Gagan_suryaputra
posts.text: Are Traditional Indicators Still Enough for Intraday Trading? — Order flow can help with timing, but it can also give misleading signals when large orders get pulled or liquidity is thin. A simple moving-average setup with disciplined exits can beat a sophisticated order-flow setup if the latter has no proven edge.

posts.text: How Can Market Profile Help You Identify Where the Market Is Likely to Reverse? — One thing I’ve noticed is that the interesting part isn’t just where price breaks out, but where it fails to sustain that move. A quick move above VAH followed by a return into value can tell us more than the breakout itself. I’d watch how price behaves around those levels rather than blindly treating them as reversal points. The shift often tells a better story than the levels themselves.

posts.author: Edwin_Marshall
posts.text: How Can I Identify the Best Elliott Wave Count for Intraday Trading? — One practical filter is the depth and duration of Wave 2 versus Wave 4. In a typical impulse, they often differ in character: one may be a sharp retracement, the other a sideways correction. If both look identical, I’d be cautious about the count. Also, Elliott Wave counts are fractal, so a move that looks like a five-wave impulse on a 5-minute chart can simply be one leg of a larger correction on the hourly chart. That’s where a lot of NIFTY wave counts go wrong.

posts.author: FVS

posts.text: Long Option Becomes ITM Only After Short Option — The problem is that physical delivery margin is charged separately on each position, regardless of whether it’s hedged or not. Even if you construct a strategy where both the long and short legs are ITM and the net delivery obligation is zero, you’ll still need to maintain the required physical delivery margin near expiry. So changing the CE/PE combination won’t really solve the margin issue.

posts.author: DishantSR
posts.text: SEBI Reworks CAS: A Win-Win for Cash and F&O Traders? — Useful summary. The practical takeaway for expiry day: from 7 Dec 2026, don’t assume the CAS print is what settles your F&O. Settlement moves to the last 30-minute VWAP of continuous trading, while the cash closing price stays CAS-based, so the two can diverge. Also note the hours: expiring index derivatives stop at 3:30, while stock derivatives and non-expiring index keep going to 3:45, and the CAS order window can close randomly between 3:38 and 3:40 — so avoid last-second edits.

posts.text: The SIF Discussion — Many SIFs play the safe game like I said, and the goal is a smoother equity curve. But they are also allowed to do unhedged naked calls/puts/fut upto 25% of total capital… Quant mutual fund’s SIFs seem to have used this nicely So there are possibilities (risk and reward), which I may have understated in my previous post… if you see the bi monthly reports, many SIFs do very little naked derivatives…

posts.author: Chetan_Nahata
posts.text: The SIF Discussion — By that logic what exactly does the SIF has over an MF? During the Bull run i’d make the guess that the MF would be the outperformer b/w the two and during the downside a probably smoother curve? Is the More Expensive version worth it?

posts.author: VijayNair
posts.text: The SIF Discussion — SIFs are not true hedge funds (atleast not how most US Hedge funds are), and for the most part the goal is to participate in equities, but with modest hedging, to smoothen the equity curve. In India SIFs are basically just guarded and diluted (less edgy?) Equity Mutual Funds. In big bull-runs, they will likely underperform the benchmark index, but other times, well managed SIFs may have a decent chance of outperformance.

posts.text: Global Investing — Yes. Non disclosure of beneficiary/custodial accounts in Schedule FA has strict flat penalty of 10L/year. posts.author: VijayNair
posts.text: The SIF Discussion — SIFs are allowed to utilise 25% unhedged derivatives. Anything not backed by shares is considered unhedged for SIFs AFAIK. Strangles/Straddles are by definition unhedged (although straddles have sort of partial hedge due to the other leg being ATM) otherwise they would be called iron flys and iron condors. I suspect most are hedged in some way - some of it could also be naked short puts to covered calls, and then they might also be short on some stocks, to balance things out.. Either way they are usually less than 15% of capital… And sometimes added diversification is good…

posts.author: Gagan_suryaputra
posts.text: When Market Understanding Becomes a Concern — I’m not suggesting that liquidity should be removed. My point is that easy liquidity can make switching in and out almost frictionless, which can encourage short-term behaviour. LTGC may reduce one reason to sell, but it doesn’t fix the underlying issue of why investors lose confidence in equities in the first place. Making people hold longer and giving them a reason to hold are two very different things.

posts.author: Gagan_suryaputra

posts.text: Why are you still trading after JaneStreet scandal? — Markets aren’t perfectly fair, and institutions have clear advantages over retail traders. If you don’t have an edge, staying out is also a smart decision.

posts.text: Troubled waters — Ok, I found something interesting which might explain the case. RBI publishes govt surplus liquidity, available for auctioning, in daily money market operations. (row H) Press Releases | Official Website of Reserve Bank of India For entire October this has been consistently shown zero. However in last couple of days, there has been jump. image 778×349 7.06 KB I have no idea why there is surplus (could be due to lot of reason) but this might be a reason why RBI just rejected on T-bill auction. If govt is already running surplus, maybe no point paying high T-bill rate this week…

posts.author: Akash_Shah
posts.text: Troubled waters — There are two ways of looking at it: This is rare event, it signals trouble (It is not, as I said previously this happens once in a while) This is happening recurringly, a trend is emerging, it signals trouble (One similar event in March, one partial in June and now one in Oct, hardly a trend, happening once in a while) I don’t think current auction rejection fits any of this yet. And hence my opinion is this is non-event. In future lot of things can happen and it can signal lot of things. That is a different discussion altogether

Lumpsum/SIP does not matter much if investment horizon is in decades. You c…

posts.author: KaranAggarwal
posts.text: Freelancers: Fixed Monthly SIP or Investing Only When Income Is Good? — Since you have irregular income from freelancing, don’t go for a large fixed amount but start with a small SIP that you can comfortably continue even in the lean months. Build up an emergency fund of 6-12 months of living expenses. Invest any extra money during high income months. Liquidity and not going broke is the primary thing, but SIP consistency matters.

posts.text: Kite Trading View Charts - Issues — Whenever the option chain is opened over the chart, the entire chart disappears.All indicators and the specific timeframe that were active on the chart are removed, and the chart opens on the default timeframe instead.If you have multiple charts open on a screen and then open and subsequently close the option chain on that same screen, all those multiple charts will disappear, and only a single chart will remain open.On platforms like Dhan and Indstocks, opening the option chain triggers a pop-up window, and when you close the option chain, the chart remains…

As price rises, the short call goes ITM first and the long call only goes ITM after price crosses the higher strike, which is where your loss stops growing. Puts: sell the higher strike put, buy a lower strike put (bull put spread). Same idea on the downside. You collect a net credit, keep all of it if price stays on the safe side of the short strik…

posts.author: Norton_Fernandes
posts.text: What is up with REIT and INVITs lately? — I think it could be a mix of factors. Housing sales haven’t been as strong as expected in some markets, which could be affecting sentiment around REITs. Interest rates are also a factor, as higher borrowing costs and refinancing risks can put pressure on returns. There are also concerns around property valuations. posts.text: How does taxation on REITs and InvITs work? — Yes, you have to adjust it manually. Brokers don’t do it. Formula: Capital gain = Sale price − (Your purchase price − ROC received on your units) Get the ROC per unit from the REIT’s distribution announcements (the “repayment of debt” component). Multiply it by your units, then subtract the total from your purchase cost. Enter the adjusted cost in your ITR’s capital gains schedule.

posts.author: Kabir_B
posts.text: Question : leading / lagging nature of certain stocks — Sometimes Nifty starts moving while quite a few stocks are still flat. A few heavyweights can move the index first, and the rest of the market may take some time to catch up. Looking at past cycles, large caps have generally held up better in weaker phases, while mid and small caps have tended to catch up much faster once the market gets into a stronger recovery. So maybe the leading and lagging behaviour is not just about individual stocks. The market cycle, sector rotation and even the way Nifty is weighted could all play a role.

If futures become more expensive to trade, some people may shift toward options without fully understanding the risks involved.
